chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad, who said:

He was asked about the ornamented sword and the iron sword that is gilded, can it be sold for dirhams? He said: Yes, and with gold. And he said: It is disliked to sell it on credit (with delay). And he said: If the price is more than the silver (value of the decoration), there is no problem.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for selling ornamented swords in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of selling decorated swords (al-sayf al-muhalla) for both gold and silver, distinguishing between immediate exchange and credit sales. It highlights the scholarly nuance that while selling on credit (nasi'ah) is generally disliked for such items, the transaction becomes permissible if the price exceeds the intrinsic silver value, reflecting the principle of avoiding riba in commodity exchanges. This ruling underscores the practical application of fiqh principles regarding the valuation of goods with both utilitarian and decorative value in Shia jurisprudence.
